Thermoluminescence detectors (TLDs) were used for dose measurements at JET during the last two weeks of the C30 experimental campaign.
Several hundred lithium fluoride detectors of various types were produced, including highly sensitive LiF:Mg,Cu,P (MCP-N) and standard LiF:Mg,Ti (MTS-N) detectors.
The MCP detectors have a much higher sensitivity to radiation compared to the MTS detectors, with a detection threshold below 1 μGy for MCP versus 20-50 μGy for MTS.
Pairs of 6LiF/7LiF detectors were used to distinguish between neutron and non-neutron components of the radiation field.
Polyethylene (PE-300) moderators were used to detect higher energy neutrons.
The TLDs were installed at 11 positions in the JET Torus Hall and labyrinth, with the measured gamma dose varying over about 5 orders of magnitude.
The neutron fluence at the experimental positions was derived from the TLD response, using a calibration in a thermal neutron field at the PTB.
The measured neutron fluence varied over more than 4 orders of magnitude, from around 10^4 n/cm^2 in positions far from the tokamak to over 10^12 n/cm^2 close to the machine.
Compared to the measurements, the MCNP calculations generally underestimated the neutron fluence close to the machine and overestimated it in positions far from the machine.
The largest discrepancies between measurements and calculations were found for the 6Li-enriched TLDs, which have the largest self-shielding effect.
Possible reasons for the discrepancies include approximations in the MCNP model, the non-thermal neutron spectrum in positions close to the tokamak, and shielding/shadowing effects between the TLDs.
The results confirm that TLD technology can be usefully applied to measurements of neutron streaming through JET Torus Hall ducts.
The experiences from this work will provide a basis for implementing TLD-based radiation monitoring in ITER to minimize personnel dose.
A previous experiment during the DTE1 campaign at JET using activation foils had obtained similar results to the TLD measurements.
The authors plan to investigate new detector positions further in the labyrinth and ducts, and improve the TLD configuration to reduce shadowing effects in future campaigns.
